tex_content.html:
Theorem
[Liouville's theorem, mean-value form]

↗ def:ball-mean-value-property ↗ thm:harnack-local-mvp

\group Harmonic Functions

Let $n\ge 1$. If $u\in C(\R ^n)$ has the ball mean-value property and is bounded below, then $u$ is constant. In particular, every bounded such function is constant.
Proof

↗ thm:harnack-local-mvp

\sketch Put $m=\inf _{\R ^n}u$ and $v=u-m\ge 0$. The local Harnack estimate is available at every scale, so $v(x)\le 2^n v(y)$ for all $x,y$. Taking the infimum over $y$ forces $v(x)=0$.

□
